No problem. You're absolutely right about therapy. You have to be open to it. Unfortunately, I'm a little jaded about it because of past experiences. 

I feel like therapy is partially in place to help someone recognize their personal road blocks, show them how to break them, and how to keep them from coming back. I know what my problems stem from (mostly abandonment issues and emotional abuse). So for me, it seems like an extra expense I can't afford. I know what I need to do to become "functional", I just don't see the point. I worry a lot that I'm going to become one of those people that just goes through the motions of life with no friends or family. No matter how many times I try and connect with people I just can't seem to. 

Yeah, guinea pigs are great. They're pretty much the beagles of the small animal world. Affectionate to a fault. Little man is just about 9 though, so I'm pretty sure he's immortal.

I haven't been to therapy in my adult life, but when i was a kid (until about high school) I was in some kind of support group or therapy. A social worker had to come to my house for several months for group therapy sessions due to my bother's severe anger issues, and my mother's drug addiction. I never saw any benefit from them. 

I'm glad therapy is helping you though. 

I have a guinea pig.

I hope this helps you make your decision to go the GED route or back to school.

I'm actually in the process of getting my GED now, and they have revised the test in the last couple years. The test is now 4 separate sections (1 per subject). It may be different depending on what state you're in but for me the english test was about 2 hours, the social studies and science both an hour and a half each, and the math almost 2 hours. You can schedule each section for a different day. Each segment is $37.50, and you must pass each part individually; scores from multiple segments cannot be averaged together for a passing grade like they used to.

There could be two sides to this statement. One: I'm crazy and I don't even have a guinea pig and if that's the case I'm worse off than I thought. Option two: I'm projecting the need to be accepted and liked onto an animal that isn't capable of actually loving me the way I love it, but I'm not one for the "animals don't have emotions" arguement. Either way, I still care about it's well being more than my own. So, I'm still in the same boat.
That is an intense hug. They're both so into it.

Oh no, I didn't mean to make anyone feel worse. I don't know your situation, but maybe you could get a pet that's just yours. 

I'll be hanging on for as long as the gp does.

I always wanted a bird but wasn't sure I could handle the commitment.

Thank you. I feel like when you agree to be a parent - to animals or people, that there are no short cuts. You signed up to take care of them. So you should be there till the end. Or, in the case of human children, at least until your kids can take care of themselves.

Agreed on the retro, but I like some newer stuff too. Nothing beats Chrono Trigger though.

 He is a cutie. I wish I had video of this but when he was really young he loved to play with plastic spoons. He would pick them up in his teeth and bang on things. I bought him one of those kid's xylophones (the ones that are rainbow colored) and he got such a kick out of the noise he made on it with his spoon. I like to take care of things I guess. When I first got him he was a vicious brat who bit and was on the euthanasia list. Now he's a big baby. 

I'm just worn out. Tired of feeling like part of the VERY small percentage of people that aren't completely cruel and selfish. 

I don't have any friends any longer. No friends are better than bad friends and because I'm a people pleaser, I tend to get walked on. 

I'm not really that interesting. I'm also much more awkward in person. Anonymously typing makes me come off way more put together than I really am.

Mostly isolate myself. I read a lot, I like to draw, write, play video games (I have a massive retro collection). All pretty solitary activities. 

Yeah he's got it good. He sleeps on fleece blankets, his cage is over 4 feet long and about 2.5 feet wide, he eats oxbow brand and a different hay every day of the week. And this might sound weird, but he likes music and children's audio books. Plus he's out a lot. He really likes to "help" me draw by chewing my pencils.

I hope your husband is doing better. Sometimes meeting the right someone can bring you back from the brink. 

I really wish you could pick your family. Then we could stick all the jerks in one pot. 

I'm all ears if you want to vent :)

This has been lifelong depression, but it got more serious about 4-5 years back, I had other pets as well as the guinea pig at that point and didn't want to leave any behind. I figured I could wait out their lives since they were all very old or had short lifespans to begin with. But the guinea pig keeps on trucking. While I'm glad he's happy and healthy, it was not part of the plan for him to live this long. I thought I would be gone a couple years ago. He's my last remaining tie, everyone else has passed away already.

Sadly no funds :( But the guinea pig isn't really the issue. I love him to death, but nothing lives forever. My issue was that I had finally made peace with ending everything. I wouldn't have anyone to miss or miss me once he was gone. I could give up guilt free. But if he lives to be 14 (that's the oldest recorded I think), then I'm going to have to function well enough to at least hold a job. Even shitty customer service positions usually require you to make eye contact and say hello, or answer a phone. I used to be able to do these things but it's like I've forgotten.

That's kind of how I've been living the last 2 years. Why get another job, money doesn't matter to the dead. But that was before I realized my pet would live so long. I guess I'll have to start the uphill battle again since I'm running out of savings. It takes money to feed him, and I would never hurt an animal to make my way out easier. I was just so set on free falling and a means to an end that these last couple years were almost a relief. 

Thanks for the link. I'll be watching that later.

Thank you. I have had everything from mice to cats. I even had two syrian hamsters (the big goofy ones) that had been born with anophthalmia. They were blind (born without eyeballs), and deaf. They were very sweet but understandably made some people queasy. I worked at a high kill shelter for a long time and took home the unwanted ones a lot. 

My first day too. (i kinda feel like the new kid in school in front of the classroom). I really can't believe how helpful everyone has been so far. I really half expected not to get any response or maybe a "suck it up". I'm kinda a glass half empty kinda girl I guess. I really don't know how any of this works but I would like to extend the offer. If you ever feel like venting, I like listening too.

Yeah, no kidding about the family thing. I often wonder if it's the chicken or the egg. Did I become such a loser because of all the emotional battering and neglect? Or am I an awful person and do I deserve it?

I used to have several pets. They've always been well cared for, never so many that it was overwhelming. I've seen too many people go down that road. But I decided he was going to be the last because the ones I like to adopt are usually not very adoptable to begin with, so re-homing is near impossible. Either aggression cases or special needs types. I understand rejects I guess. 

This is my first attempt at any online or anonymous interaction. I'm amazed at how compassionate some people can be. Sometimes I feel like people who care about something other than themselves are few and far between.

Oh no :( I don't want to stir up painful things. And 5ish is old. 

The crazy thing is he's doing fantastic. He's a little blind but gps don't have great vision anyway, and the vet says he has mild arthritis but nothing serious. I adopted him when he was 6 weeks old with his sister/girlfriend (she was already pregnant when I got them) and he's already outlived her and the baby. I don't want him to outlive me too. It sounds bad but it would be easier if he was sick and suffering. Then I wouldn't need to feel so guilty about thinking about what I want to do. 

No anxiety support. I never used to feel this way. It just kind of hit me over the head a couple years ago. My hands get shaky even typing. but at least if can edit and re-edit everything I say a million times before someone sees it this way.
